claim: On the Next a game or ISR write to port 7FFD can remap the MMU slots holding hook code or a hook stack, so use a slot the write does not reset and check ROM and paging state at hook entry and exit.

evidence.text: Return (8F4E) maps the hook page back because a 7FFD write maps ROM over slot 1.
evidence.quote: return (8F4E) maps the hook page back (7FFD maps ROM over slot 1)

evidence.text: A hook window into another bank uses MMU slot 2, because the music handler's 7FFD write resets MMU 0, 1, 6 and 7.
evidence.quote: Window: MMU slot 2, because the music handler's 7FFD write resets

evidence.text: The original's paging writes replace MMU1, so a forwarded music ISR cannot retain a private stack in MMU1; a separate stack in spare page 25 / MMU2 survives those writes.
evidence.quote: cannot retain a private stack at3Exx. A separate stack in spare page25/MMU2 survives those writes;

evidence.text: A wrapper mapping slot 1 to ROM crashed when the hook stack was in slot 1; restore what was found.
evidence.quote: A wrapper that mapped slot 1 to ROM during the interrupt crashed when a hook's stack was in slot 1. It now restores what it found.

evidence.text: A 7FFD write inside w_go (paging bank 1 for a W range) put ROM back into MMU slot 0: 51 characters printed for 18 and each update ran 3 frames long; the verifier's NextMem models the reset now.
evidence.quote: A 7FFD write inside w_go (paging bank 1 for a W range) put ROM back into MMU slot 0, so the save went to ROM and the restore read ROM
